items.prompt:
About how much energy passes to the next level of a food chain?
A) About 10 percent
B) About 90 percent
C) All of it
D) None

Producers in an ecosystem are usually
A) plants that make their own food
B) top predators
C) rocks
D) decomposers only
items.answer: A) plants that make their own food

steps: Producers make food and capture energy.

items.prompt:
As you go up a food chain, available energy
A) increases
B) decreases
C) stays the same
D) disappears instantly

steps: Energy decreases at each higher level.

items.prompt:
Plants capture 10,000 units of energy. About how much reaches the plant-eaters?
A) 10,000
B) 1,000
C) 100
D) 0

In an energy pyramid, the widest level is the
A) top
B) bottom (producers)
C) middle
D) there is no widest

Why are there fewer top predators than plants?
A) Little energy reaches the top of the food chain
B) Predators do not eat
C) Plants are predators
D) Energy increases upward
items.answer: A) Little energy reaches the top of the food chain

steps: Energy drops at each level, supporting few predators.

items.prompt:
If a top predator receives about 100 units, the producers captured about
A) 100
B) 1,000
C) 10,000
D) 10

steps: Multiply by about 10 per level down the chain.

items.prompt:
Only about 10 percent of energy passes up a food chain because
A) most energy is used for life processes or lost as heat
B) energy is destroyed
C) energy is created
D) all energy passes on
items.answer: A) most energy is used for life processes or lost as heat

steps: Energy is lost at each step.
